I was born and raised in a small town nestled in the rolling hills of the countryside. My parents, both educators, instilled in me a deep love for learning and an appreciation for the natural world. As a child, I could often be found exploring the woods behind our house, discovering new plants and animals, and trying to identify every bird I heard.

In high school, I developed a passion for literature and language, which led me to pursue a degree in English at the university level. During my undergraduate studies, I discovered a talent for creative writing and decided to continue my education by pursuing a Master of Fine Arts in Creative Writing. It was during these years that I began to hone my craft as a writer, experimenting with various genres and forms, and developing my own unique voice.

After graduating, I spent several years working as a freelance writer, contributing articles to local and national publications, and building a reputation as a skilled and insightful journalist. However, I eventually felt called to return to teaching, and I accepted a position at a small liberal arts college in my hometown. There, I have been able to combine my love of writing and my passion for education, inspiring students to explore their creativity and find their own voices.

In my free time, I still enjoy spending time in nature, taking long walks with my dog, and practicing yoga. I am also an avid reader and try to stay up-to-date on the latest literary trends and movements. Over the years, I have built a strong community of fellow writers and artists, and I regularly attend conferences and workshops to continue growing and learning.

Looking back on my journey so far, I am grateful for the opportunities I have had to explore my passions and develop my skills. I am excited to see what the future holds and am committed to continuing to learn and grow as a writer, teacher, and human being.
